title: A name that reads like a Net term may carry a different rule
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Choose names for term A and term B that read like Net terms but are not standard terms.
  • Start on the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click "New Credit Term".
  2. Type the name of term A in Name.
  3. Click the Day box.
  4. Type 25 in the Day box.
  5. Click "Create Credit Term".
  6. Click "New Credit Term".
  7. Type the name of term B in Name.
  8. Type 14 in the Days box.
  9. Click "Create Credit Term".
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The "New Credit Term" window opens.

Step 2:

  • No message shows under Name.

Step 3:

  • "Due day of the following month" is chosen.

Step 4:

  • The blue information line shows below the options.

Step 5:

  • The term A is created.
  • Its Due column reads "25th of the following month" (the rule, not the name).

Step 6:

  • The "New Credit Term" window opens.

Step 7:

  • No message shows under Name.

Step 8:

  • The blue information line shows below the options.

Step 9:

  • The toast "term B created" shows.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11672 (Story 3, Create or edit a credit term)

  • S3-E1: “A name that reads like a standard term but is not one (for example "Net 14", "Net 10", "Net 6") is allowed. The name and the rule are independent: a term named "Net 6" may be due on the 25th of the following month. The Due column always shows the rule.”
  • Key Decisions: “Shops name their terms freely; the Due column always shows the rule. A term named "Net 6" may be due on the 25th of the following month (S3-E1).”
